---
title: biblint
---

`biblint` is a deterministic Rust linter and formatter for BibTeX.
It is designed for the post-edit pass in agentic workflows: formatting fixes are repeatable, while semantic observations such as duplicate records remain visible diagnostics.

## Commands

```console
biblint check .
biblint check references.bib --fix
biblint check references.bib --fix --unsafe-fixes
biblint check . --output json
biblint format references.bib
biblint format . --check
biblint format references.bib --diff
biblint rule
biblint rule duplicate_key
```

`check` reports syntax, lint, and formatting diagnostics.
`format` only formats files; `format --check` reports whether a file would change, and `format --diff` prints the change without writing it.

Both commands accept explicit files, directories, and standard input (`-`).
A directory contributes `.bib` files recursively.
See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for file discovery and policy selection.

## Default behavior

With no configuration file, biblint:

- uses two spaces for field indentation;
- writes fields as `field = value` with one space on each side of `=`;
- lowercases entry types and field names;
- preserves field order and value spelling;
- reports syntax errors, duplicate keys and fields, missing keys, empty fields, unsupported escapes, unsupported source, and formatting differences.

Alignment, sorting, cleanup, value transforms, duplicate analysis beyond keys, and key-format checking are configured explicitly.
There are no formatter policy switches on the command line; commit `biblint.toml` so local and CI runs share the same policy.

## Design

The formatter changes the structured BibTeX syntax it understands.
Source it cannot safely interpret is preserved and reported as an `unsupported_construct` note.
Diagnostics carry source locations and, where a safe or configured transform is available, a fix.

The default workflow is deliberately conservative:

```console
biblint check .
biblint check . --fix
```

The first command observes.
The second applies safe canonical formatting.
Use `--unsafe-fixes` only when the checked-in configuration enables transforms that can change content or identity, such as key generation, merging, field removal, brace removal, or author truncation.
